0x80081868.name: bind_forward

The two halves of that word are swapped by the time PadRead returns it, so 0x1000 is UP and 0x0800 is START. Four independent uses say so: the slot holding 0x0800 is read only by the pause menu, the one holding 0x0100 opens the map, play_movie skips a movie on 0x10/0x20/0x40/0x80 -- the four face buttons -- and everything on 0x800, and the title menu confirms on 0x20/0x40/0x800 and moves its cursor on 0x1000/0x4000. Under the raw reading those are, in order, R1 opening the menu, L2 the map, the four directions skipping a movie, and the cursor moving on TRIANGLE and CROSS

The first guess, 0x801b2614, reads zero for a whole session and is wrong. POSITIVE IS UP: the resting -190 was read as a downward tilt and the port was built on that, and a player looking up saw it look down

0x80040ae4.name: render_walk
0x80040ae4.evidence: two loops, not one. The first steps the ACTOR table at 0x80185da8 by 0x88 for 200 slots and draws a creature only when its +9 is 1; its model number is the mesh byte at +1 plus 0x80. The second steps object_table by 0x44 for 396 slots, skips a u16 type id of 0xff, clears bit 0x80 of +3 every frame and dispatches on the class byte at +4 -- 0xe9 and 0xe5 are skipped, 0x1f, 0xf0 and 0xf2 each have their own path. The old name here was object_walk, which described only the second half. For everything else the draw test is view_bits_at(position) & record +0, or type flag +3 bit 8 to draw regardless: every visible cell's view byte carries 2, which a placed record's +0 is, so an arm that zeroes +0 -- classes 0x0b, 0x14, 0x15, 0x1f, 0x59, 0x5f, 0xe0 to 0xe4, 0xe6, 0xe7 and 0xea, and whatever opcode 9 names -- hides the object

_note_object_model.name: object type -> model

The 128 was MEASURED, not reasoned: a player stood in the game beside the port and named four pairs off the model gallery -- helmet type 34 = model 162, healing grass 104 = 232, save point 227 = 355, bull's head 253 = 381 -- and all four differ by exactly 128. The sizes agree: the grass is 384x211x416 under the rule where MO.T[type] gave it 4176x4096x3808, which is what the player saw as a big white thing. MO.T[type], the previous assumption, had never been checked against anything
